stories.title: Local boy with rare disease designs cleats for Browns' Jerry Jeudy
stories.summary: Allan Mulloy, a 15-year-old from Champion who lives with a rare disease, got to design cleats for the Browns' Jerry Jeudy to wear at an upcoming game. When he was 7 years old, Allan was diagnosed with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), a rare genetic muscle condition that eventually leads to losing the ability to walk. It also affects breathing muscles, the heart and life expectancy, said Dr. Matthew Ginsberg , pediatric neurologist with Akron Children's Hospital . Today, Allan uses a power chair to get around, but he isn't in a chair full time, as he can still walk short distances. When other kids ask him about his condition, he tells them what he can do instead of what he can't.

stories.title: Exclusive: Bots amplified conspiracy theories and panic about recent tech outages
stories.summary: Bot accounts have helped spread conspiracy theories about a wave of major tech outages over the last week, according to new research shared exclusively with Axios. Why it matters: Purveyors of disinformation appear to be exploiting public anxiety over the cyberattacks and fragile infrastructure, amplifying suspicions of coordinated cyberattacks and government cover-ups. While it's unclear who's behind these accounts, the pattern shows that when technology failures lack substantive explanations, bot networks will fill the void to manufacture panic. Catch up quick: Microsoft, Apple, JPMorgan Chase, United, Workday, the Federal Aviation Administration and the National Security Agency each faced outages over the last week. Then came the conspiracy theories: When the FAA grounded flights for four hours Friday, people were quick to assume it was tied to the rollout of an AI tool at the agency.

The sale of Châtaigniers en fleurs ("Chestnut Trees in Blossom") shatters the renowned artist's previous auction record of $117.2 million set in 2022. The historic sale in New York on Wednesday comes after an eleventh-hour agreement was reached to resolve a dispute regarding claims the art piece was previously sold under duress during the rise of the Nazis.

stories.summary: Why do rich powerful men love golf? Ultimately the sport exists in a world where the politics is assumed to be settled F arewell, then, LIV Golf . As its original figurehead Greg Norman once so delicately put it, albeit in a slightly different context: we’ve all made mistakes, you learn from those mistakes, and you move forward.
